The son of Nigerian journalist Kemi Olunloyo, Olukayode Taiwo, has been arrested in Connecticut, United States, over allegations involving a firearm in Pennsylvania. Olunloyo confirmed that Taiwo is her son in a statement shared on Friday, saying, “My son Olukayode Joshua Taiwo has been found by the US law enforcement team who declared him wanted. Thank you for all your prayers and concern.” Taiwo was arrested on Thursday night by the US Marshals and Newington police after a search operation at Millyard at Meadows Commons Apartments on Pane Road in Newington, according to FOX 61 on Friday. The arrest prompted authorities to order nearby apartment residents to remain indoors during the operation. According to the police report, the US Marshals “was conducting an investigation into Olukayode Joshua Taiwo, 26, of Philadelphia.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources It added that he “was wanted out of Pennsylvania for charges related to an incident involving a firearm”. The US Marshals, assisted by Newington police, responded to the apartment complex on Thursday evening to search for him. “A shelter in place warning was issued to apartment residents, and the public was asked to avoid the area,” the report stated. He was taken into custody without incident, according to police. Newington police arrested him as a fugitive from justice and held him on a $1m bond. “He is scheduled to appear in court on Friday,” the report added. It was not immediately clear when Taiwo would be returned to Pennsylvania to face the outstanding charges. PUNCH had earlier reported that Philadelphia police were searching for him over the alleged abduction of a 23-year-old woman at gunpoint on November 2. Investigators said he was also suspected of shooting at the same woman near her home on November 15. Christabel Ndoeche
